title: Safe plan executor and SDK apply guards for Optimize automation
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Optimize recommendations include batching and KV-caching configuration changes that can materially affect cost and latency. We need API+SDK primitives and a server-side plan-executor that make applying those recommendations safe to retry, observable, and reversible. Current ad-hoc apply flows risk double-applying, partial failures (half-applied config), and poor operator UX when retries or rollbacks are required.

Goal: Implement a Plan Executor service and corresponding REST endpoints plus SDK helpers to support: 1) staging a deterministic plan, 2) idempotent apply semantics with operation tokens and optimistic fencing, 3) a safe rollback/replay path, 4) a webhook handshake for downstream systems and observability hooks. This ticket covers the API surface, server behavior, SDK ergonomics, and migration tasks.

Design Summary:
- New endpoints: POST /optimize/plans (create+validate plan, returns plan_id), POST /optimize/plans/{plan_id}/apply (start apply, accepts client_operation_id, dry_run flag), POST /optimize/plans/{plan_id}/rollback (trigger rollback), GET /optimize/plans/{plan_id}/status.
- Idempotency model: client supplies client_operation_id (UUID). Server persists an operation record and returns an operation_token. If the same client_operation_id is retried, the server will return the canonical operation result. Applies are assigned monotonically increasing apply_sequence numbers for the target resource to avoid reordering.
- Fencing and concurrency: Each plan execution is serialized per target (pool/model-route) using an optimistic lock: apply_sequence and operation_token checks. Concurrent attempts get 409 with a retry-after and the last-applied sequence.
- Webhook handshake: /webhooks/optimize will be used for notifications. On apply start server emits a 'plan.apply.pending' webhook; webhook consumer must ack within TTL to move to 'pending-ack' -> 'applied'. If ack fails or consumer returns non-2xx, Plan Executor moves the operation into DLQ and marks apply as 'needs-attention' (UI shows a reversible apply).
- Safe rollback: Rollback path is the inverse plan derived from an immutable audit log. Rollbacks are also idempotent and require client_operation_id. A dry_run mode returns the diff without committing.
- SDK: Add OptimizeClient.apply_plan(plan_id, *, client_operation_id=None, dry_run=False, retry_policy=...) which manages operation_id generation, automatic exponential backoff on 409/5xx, and exposes the canonical operation token and final status. SDK will also expose utility to subscribe to webhooks for local testing (dev mode).

Acceptance criteria:
- API spec reviewed and merged in docs repo (link in comments).
- Server persists operation records and enforces idempotency for retries from clients.
- SDK implements helper with documented retry semantics and unit tests.
- UI shows plan state transitions with links to operation logs and rollback button when needed.
- Security review completed for webhook auth and operation record retention.

Non-goals: complex multi-target transactions (will be handled by higher-level composition ticket), automatic greedy rollback without operator confirmation.

Risks & trade-offs:
- Strong idempotency requires an operation history which increases storage and retention needs; we will garbage-collect records older than retention window.
- Webhook ack TTL adds latency to commit; we will make this configurable per workspace.
- Forcing strict serialization can reduce throughput for high-frequency small adjustments; we will offer a 'best-effort' apply mode later if needed.

Next steps / Implementation plan:
1) Finalize API contract and open PR for server changes (ETA: 3 days).
2) Implement operation store (immutable append-only table) + GC policy (ETA: 1 sprint).
3) Implement Plan Executor state machine and webhook emission + DLQ (ETA: 1 sprint).
4) SDK helpers and integration tests (ETA: 1 sprint).
5) Console UX + rollout gating (ETA: next cycle).

Related docs and artifacts: Design doc: https://docs.redwood-inference.com/optimize/plan-executor-design (internal). Server PR template: https://github.com/redwood-inference/optimize/pull/421. SDK spike branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/compare/optimize-apply-spike.
